summary: Pascal Rochat, founder of Active Niche Funds, discusses the solar energy revolution, highlighting that solar costs have dropped by 90% from 2009-2019, making it the cheapest electricity source globally. He explains the massive growth trajectory from 240 GW to potentially 1 TW by 2030, with solar expected to reach 23-25% of world electricity generation by 2030. The conversation covers challenges, opportunities, and the Active Solar Fund's investment approach across the entire solar value chain, with emphasis on the big story of energy transition rather than individual stock picking.
key_takeaways: Solar electricity costs dropped 90% between 2009-2019, making it the cheapest source at 2-4 cents/kWh
Solar installations expected to grow from 240 GW in 2022 to 1 TW annually before 2030
60% of all new power capacity installed globally is now solar
Solar expected to generate 23-25% of world electricity by 2030, becoming the primary source
Individual solar companies carry significant risk despite strong sector fundamentals
Energy transition creates opportunity across entire value chain, not just panel manufacturers
